title: Rav Ulla bar Abba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman calls him a very pious man. [Sanhedrin 88b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.88b.9) relates that they sent from there: “Who merits the world to come? One who is humble and lowly, enters modestly and leaves modestly, studies Torah constantly, and takes no credit for himself.” The sages directed their attention to Rav Ulla bar Abba.

In Hyman’s account of [Ketubot 74a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.74a.10), Rav Ulla bar Abba speaks in Ulla’s name, and Ulla speaks in the name of R-H [אר״ה]. If so, Hyman places him approximately in the fourth generation of the Babylonian Amoraim.[^1]

notes.text: The notice begins on [printed p. 974](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=141) and ends on [p. 975](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=142) with the abbreviation אר״ה. Ketubot gives Rav Ulla bar Abba speaking in the name of Ulla, who speaks in the name of Rabbi Elazar. Hyman’s approximate dating depends on the chain as he reads it.
